title: Volume 2 Chapter 1: To You Whom I Can Reach with My Hand, But Whose Voice Cannot Reach Me 1
content: "Today is another day of Adventurer Life!"
Even after being falsely accused and exiled from her hometown, and now facing a fake marriage with a man she doesn't even like, Erika Solnzali remained Erika Solnzali.
──In other words, she was noble and beautiful, laughing in the face of adversity and crushing it beneath her feet.
That was the kind of person she was.
"Weren't you supposed to take a break today?"
I asked, threading a needle through the hole in my shirt that had been torn by a dragon's claw just days ago. Growing up poor had made me skilled at sewing.
Erika, who had said she had something to do in her room, looked at my shabby self for a brief moment with a perplexed expression.
As her fake husband, I couldn't help but worry that she might be disillusioned by seeing my poverty.
Dressed in her usual adventurer's inner wear topped with a white shirt, Erika gazed at me with curiosity.
By the way, there wasn't a single wrinkle on her shirt. No one would believe that she had only recently learned how to iron. She was already better at it than I was, who had taught her.
I see, Erika nodded slightly.
"I heard you were sewing. Are you repairing your gear? You really can do anything."
I felt a sense of relief inside that her words didn't carry a hint of disappointment.
"Adventurer gear is expensive... well, it's a necessity, I guess."
I barely managed to suppress the urge to say it was because I was poor.
"If that's the case, then today is impossible."
Erika's face fell, looking disappointed.
"Impossible" meant that we wouldn't be going out to hunt monsters today.

Just yesterday, we had fought a massive Forest Dragon, as large as a castle. It wouldn't be surprising for a normal adventurer to take a couple of days off afterward, but this was Erika we're talking about.
"What is that look on your face?"
She tilted her head, looking at me.
That's when I realized I was smiling.
"Well, you see..."
I quickly secured the thread while shrugging my shoulders.
"I heard from an adventurer I know."
"What did you hear?"
"That there's nothing cuter than a wife's whims."
I swiftly put the needle and thread back into the sewing box.
"But since I went through the trouble of making lunch, let's eat that first, shall we?"
It had been a while since I cooked a meal outside, and I had gotten a bit carried away. It would be a waste to let it go to waste.
As I stood up from the sofa and gestured for Erika to follow me to the table, for some reason, she turned her face away from me.
"Erika?"
When I tilted my head in confusion at her strange reaction, Erika waved her hand at me, as if to say "go away."

It looked like she was trying to send a breeze to my face... or was it a gesture telling me to leave? How far should I go? I hoped it wouldn't be to the ends of the earth, but if that was no good, maybe I should cross the sea.
"Shin."
Erika's serious voice made my spine straighten.
"Even when there are only two of us, we must approach with a mindset of Constant Battle Preparedness... is that what you're saying?"
Why would I need to be in a mindset of Constant Battle Preparedness when I'm with Erika? Is she suggesting I approach this farce of a fake marriage with that mindset?

Indeed, this farce was designed to keep the heart of the Light Priestess clear. Considering the worst-case scenario, it could lead to the downfall of my homeland, so it didn't seem wrong to face this farce with a mindset of Constant Battle Preparedness.
Suppressing my confusion, I nodded as if overwhelmed by her words, and she laughed.
It was a truly challenging smile, filled with a confidence that bordered on arrogance.
"Yes, that would be fine. I wasn't prepared enough."
Her red hair, like spun fire, flickered in the sunlight streaming into the room, and her emerald eyes narrowed in delight.
The exiled marquis daughter said,
[img]https://i.imgur.com/KyfGDd3.jpeg
"I have also made up my mind, my husband."
At her unexpected "my husband," I could only nod in response.

Comsas Dortwill, the lord of the Makikomaru Claw Border Barony, was sitting in his mansion in Hekatai, holding his head in his hands. This was due to reading the report that had come up from the Adventurer Guild last night. Why had he thought it could wait until tomorrow morning?
Comsas regretted it; as a result, his mood had been terrible since morning.

He knew that the marquis daughter who had been exiled from the Faltarl Kingdom had arrived in Hekatai. He had also heard that the man accompanying her was either her bodyguard or her partner in this farce.
However, he had not heard that the two of them were adventurers capable of defeating three Golden Ogres without a scratch.
Comsas sighed as he reread the report from the guild on his desk.
In the Kingdom of Orukura, Comsas was a significant figure.
As a border baron, responsible for the border with the Demon Realm, he was effectively a king in his territory, only lacking the title.
Unlike the centralized Faltarl Kingdom, the Orukura Kingdom was a confederation, holding military power second only to the royal family.
Furthermore, due to its proximity to the Demon Realm, monsters frequently appeared.
While this caused various damages, it also brought considerable wealth to the Makikomaru Claw Barony.
Without a doubt, he was a significant figure in the Orukura Kingdom.
However, he was distanced from central politics.
To be precise, he had no time to engage in central politics, but personally, he was grateful to be away from the court's struggles.
Comsas was simply not good at the intricacies of nobility.
He despised the backstabbing and the complicated games of nobles, where one would smile at someone they had just stabbed in the back.
He sincerely believed that everyone should just say they dislike those they dislike and smile at those they like.
However, this time, being distanced from the center had turned out poorly.
He knew the general outline of the exiled marquis daughter but had not been informed of the details, nor had he sought to learn them.
If he had been a bit closer to the center, he would have naturally heard more, but unfortunately, due to his lack of friends, his knowledge had not progressed beyond the basics.
For someone like Comsas, who was timid, anxious, and extremely weak to surprises and unpreparedness, this was a rare instance of negligence.

Because of his nature, he had been away from the central politics where he could be stabbed in the back without knowing the cause. However, he should have been more cautious about what was being pushed onto him from the center.
Comsas regretted it now.
But conversely, thanks to his nature, he had managed to do well as a border baron.
His cautious personality allowed him to maintain a partnership with the Adventurer Guild, which would raise eyebrows among other nobles.
Comsas was a realist, fully aware that he was timid and not a particularly remarkable person.
He had no interest in the delicate relationship between the nobility and the common adventurers.
In the Makikomaru Claw Barony, which bordered the Demon Realm, he couldn't afford to care.
However, Comsas thought to himself.
For reports that would surprise people, he wished for a bit more thoughtful wording that wouldn't shock him.
Comsas sighed.
He heard that the two of them were only sixteen years old.
The male had apparently been a rank 4 adventurer in the Faltarl Kingdom, but even so, it was absurd to think that two of them could defeat three Golden Ogres.
While it was said that Faltarl's adventurers should add two ranks, even considering that, it was still strange.

Although the frequency of monster appearances was low, the Faltarl Kingdom was known for having powerful monsters. As a result, while there were few, the adventurers from that country were all formidable.
Even so, it was incomprehensible that a noble who hadn't even graduated from the academy could achieve such feats.
Normally, an increase in capable adventurers would be a cause for great joy for both the Makikomaru Claw Barony and the city of Hekatai.
However, the issue was that these two were the ones in question.
Comsas had only thought that the exiled noble daughter would quietly live in his city.
He never imagined that she would be an adventurer capable of such incomprehensible feats.
It was truly baffling.
Hadn't she been exiled for attempting to assassinate the Light Priestess?
He didn't know the truth of the matter, but wouldn't a noble with such a charge typically lay low after being exiled? Hadn't she narrowly avoided execution after some trouble with the Church?
With such flamboyant actions, he couldn't predict how the Church would respond.
As he began to think, his stomach started to ache.
Would the Church leave these two alone?
Certainly, defeating three Golden Ogres was an impressive achievement. However, it wasn't earth-shattering.
If that were the case, would it be alright? Or would they come to speak to him about it?
He didn't want that... Comsas thought honestly.
He slumped his slightly plump body lazily onto the desk.
He didn't want to think about anything anymore, and just then, there was a knock at the door.
From the way they knocked, he could tell who it was. Comsas remained face down on the desk and said, "Come in."
He could sense the butler entering with an exasperated expression without even looking up.
He didn't care; Comsas didn't even lift his head.
"Sir, I have an additional report from the Adventurer Guild."
Reluctantly, he raised his face. He couldn't ignore a report after all.
He was receiving a report that he had no obligation to accept. Comsas wanted to be sincere about the work of others. He didn't want to be a lord who couldn't even manage that.
Still, an additional report was unusual. Something must have happened. If it were an emergency, they would have sent a messenger directly, so he assumed it was after the fact.
Comsas glanced at the butler, silently asking what was going on, but received a shake of the head in response.
Guess he had to check for himself.
Comsas took the report on the tray and began to read.
Earlier, he had thought they should write a more considerate message, but the concise report from the guild, which conveyed only the main points, was to Comsas's liking.
And then Comsas shouted.
"Why does it say they defeated a Forest Dragon after being exiled!?"
He really wished for some consideration, Comsas thought, rubbing his painfully aching stomach.

Having been falsely accused of plotting to assassinate the Light Priestess in the Faltarl Kingdom and exiled for it, I, who had been chosen as a fake elopement partner, was walking through the city feeling quite refreshed.
The place where Erika and I had been exiled to was the double-walled city of Hekatai.
Also known as the Adventurer City, it was a place that bordered the Demon Realm, where monsters swarmed. To make use of the limited land, tall buildings were densely packed together.
It was a familiar sight from my hometown of Faltarl, but the biggest difference was that armed adventurers walked around the city without a care. And there were a lot of them.
Compared to that, the fact that the city was protected by double barriers was a minor detail. Most nobles disliked having armed commoners in the streets.
I, who was still technically a noble, was walking through such a city, and the reason I was in such a good mood was that my future was bright.
Being exiled and having a bright future sounds odd, but the fact is, I am now Erika's husband. Even if it's just for this farce, a husband is still a husband.
That means I'm the strongest. Well, for a year at least.
As Erika and I walked down the main street, filled with armed commoners, we headed towards the Adventurer Guild.

Since it was past noon, there probably wouldn't be any decent requests left, but Erika's wish was for an Adventurer Life. I thought it was important to keep our promises. If there weren't any, we could just head outside the city and hunt monsters.
"So, is there a good request available?"
In response to my straightforward question, the guild staff member, Lana, hesitated for a moment before saying,
"Lord Longdagger, are you familiar with the phrase 'Come back the day after tomorrow'?"
Knowing her initial nervousness made her sharpness feel pleasant.
It seemed that the report of our recent Forest Dragon hunt had changed something in her, and she was no longer holding back.
The Adventurer Guild in our homeland of Faltarl was rather cold, or rather, it was filled with outrageous adventurers... mainly my master, which made their reactions dull.
In contrast, Lana's fresh reactions were quite nice.
"Why do you look so satisfied? It's kind of scary."
As she neatly stacked a pile of documents at the counter, Lana displayed her wariness.
"Please check the bulletin board for requests."
"I already checked. There were only short-term labor requests throughout the city."
Well, that's to be expected, Lana murmured, showing no willingness to engage. It was probably their fault for being late. This was how all guilds operated.
Guilds do not treat specific adventurers as special. Even with my master, it was the same, let alone with me.
By the way, adventurers also serve as a balancing force in the city's labor market. Some adventurers don't even leave the city.
"It will be like this until the commotion settles down."
Ignoring Lana's cryptic remarks, which seemed to hint at something, I continued.
"I thought there might be a request for a nice group of Ogres or something."
[img]https://i.imgur.com/gcXtEpU.jpeg
"Do you have a grudge against the border baron?"
Lana's expression, as if she were saying "What are you talking about?" pierced me.
──Then, Lana seemed to realize something and looked at me with a doubtful expression, as if to say, "No way?"
"Is it really okay to be so relaxed here?"
I tilted my head at Lana's words.
"I don't know how it was in Faltarl—"
Just as Lana was about to continue her sentence, the small door, disproportionate to the massive Adventurer Guild building, swung open with great force.
The person who opened it must have been quite flustered, as the sound reached even the distant counter.
"There you are!"
The one who burst through the door and shouted was none other than Shara Ransura, the blonde Sister.
"Lord Longdagger?"
Lana's voice turned icy.
"Your wife looks quite upset... If you're going to cut fingers, please do it outside the guild."
I was too scared to turn around.
The fear of my life collapsing due to a thoughtless remark.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/XayyLhb.jpeg
Having thoroughly experienced that, I tried to grab the face of the blonde Sister who had caused me to feel that way, but she skillfully dodged.
That sneaky move of hiding behind Erika was unfair.
"That's why! This isn't the time for this!"
The name of the blonde girl shouting from behind Erika was Shara Ransura.

She was a member of the Church, whose sole doctrine was the salvation of the weak, and she was a rather unfortunate character who had been expelled from her faction for being terrible at Healing Magic.
While I appreciated her guts to fight monsters for the villagers even in a state where her ribs were sticking out, it was a shame that she called herself a Healing Faction member.
Was there no one in the Church?
When I tried to grab Shara's head as it peeked out from behind Erika, she let out a "Hya!" and pulled her youthful face back.
Surprisingly nimble.
As I clicked my tongue inwardly, my eyes, which could see magical power, caught a glimpse of her emotions. The magical power accompanying her gaze was surprisingly expressive.
"That's right."
Lana sighed in agreement with Shara's protest of "This isn't the time for this!"
I held back the urge to say, "You're the one to say that."
If you hadn't used your words thoughtlessly, we could have gotten to the main topic much sooner.
How many times do you think I shook my head at Erika, who was looking at me with cold eyes?
The centrifugal force made both my eyes... let's not go there; the image is terrible.

I wouldn't do anything that would make my wife jealous, nor do I have a face that would succeed in such a thing. The look Erika was giving me, filled with suspicion, was something that would haunt my dreams.
"Hurry up and take responsibility! Go retrieve the magic stone from the Forest Dragon!"
Shara's words made me think she could have just said that from the start, and I looked at Erika's face. For a brief moment, she seemed to consider something before returning a smile.
In other words, it was a free pass.
"I don't want to; it's a hassle."
Shara made a face like "Wee!" in response to my answer. Her facial expressions were always amusing.
"While fighting monsters is one thing, searching for a magic stone buried in the ground is just a hassle."
"Because you left it unattended, the Church is about to be overwhelmed with injured adventurers since morning!"
Even so, I scratched my head and thought.
To summarize what Shara was saying:

I had mentioned in the guild that I left a magic stone from the defeated Forest Dragon in the Demon Realm. As a result, even adventurers who usually only took on city requests were flocking to search for the magic stone, and naturally, they were getting injured and brought to the Church.
No wonder the bulletin board was overflowing with short-term labor requests.
And as for me, I felt like I couldn't care less about it.
"I'll confirm this, but the materials and magic stones left by adventurers belong to whoever picks them up, right?"
"Of course. I thought you were acting unusually calm, so I wondered if it was different in Faltarl."
"In Faltarl, anything left unattended is fair game."
As I replied to Lana, I recalled the adventurers who had followed my master to gather the scraps of magic stones he left behind. They were commonly referred to as "scrap collectors."
In other words, those extreme fools were probably charging into the Demon Realm.
Imagining the Church being overwhelmed by adventurers made me feel a bit sympathetic.
Serves them right for labeling Erika as an attempted assassin of the Light Priestess.
"Hey! Why do you look so pleased!? The Church is in trouble!"
It seemed my true feelings had shown on my face.
I quickly tried to cover it up.
"Even if you say that, the world of adventurers is one of personal responsibility."
Right? I asked Lana with just a glance.
"Well, as someone from an organization that manages adventurers, I must agree with what you said, Lord Shin."
Impressive, it's like we can read each other's minds, though I wasn't pleased about it.
"I can't say not to do it. The recommended ranks on requests are also a way of saying 'please don't die unnecessarily.'"
"Speaking of which, I remember there were recommended ranks, though I never paid attention to them."
Shara and Lana looked at me with strange expressions, while Erika nodded in satisfaction for some reason.
Since my master was someone who didn't care about such things, I had naturally become the same.
Lana sighed as if to change the subject.
"Well, putting aside the fact that 'Lord Longdagger' is out of his league, the Adventurer Guild is indeed concerned about the situation."
That was an unpleasant way to phrase it; it seemed all guilds were the same in such times.
I couldn't help but frown.
"You're really pushing it, aren't you?"
"The guild master, who is bald... I mean, the guild head, taught me to provoke adventurers."
